pr_title: Fix number parsing with negative sign
pr_body:
Fixes #47524

This change allow parsing negative numbers written with the hyphen character `-` when using cultures with negative sign not hyphen but it is one of the alternative Unicode minus sign characters. 
I have done some basic perf testing with this change and didn't notice any noticeable change.

issue_context.title: Swedish locale, NumberFormat.NegativeSign from ICU ignores parseLenient data from CLDR
issue_context.body:
### Description

Since .Net 5.0 in combination with Win10 May 2019 Update (build 18362) and later, ICU instead of NLS is used as source for locale data if I understand it correctly.

This causes issues with the negative sign using a Swedish locale, which then gets changed from Unicode 'Hyphen-Minus' to 'Minus Sign'. This actually does look good until you realize that you don't have 'Minus Sign' on a swedish keyboard, you only have 'Hyphen-Minus'. Users of our applications can therefore never enter negative numbers in any application since this change.

This would not be a problem if .Net 5.0 or the ICU library on windows respected the '[parseLenient](https://unicode-org.atlassian.net/browse/CLDR-10779?jql=text%20~%20%22sv%20minus%20sign%22)' data array that is associated with this from CLDR, as this includes the 'Hyphen-Minus'. However a strict equality seems to be used instead and 'Hyphen-Minus' can no longer be used to describe a negative number. 

Can this be fixed in the .Net runtime, or is this an underlying issue with the ICU library on Windows?

Related issue: #44678
Related issue: #40922

### Configuration
Win10 May 2019 Update (build 18362) and later.
with .Net 5.0 or later

### Workaround
Force usage of NLS instead of ICU
`<ItemGroup>`
`    <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Globalization.UseNls" Value="true" />`
`</ItemGroup>`

@tedpar I'll take more deeper look and get back to you. Thanks for reporting the issue.

> #40922

Thanks, yes, that issue you referenced mentions the same underlying problem, however that issue only deals with this by allowing overriding the default value of NumberFormat.NegativeSign. The proper fix would be to adhere to CLDR parseLenient data, which allows multiple characters to be used as negative sign when parsing from text to numbers.

review_comments:
BigInteger has an old copy of the parsing code:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Globalization/FormatProvider.Number.cs
There's an issue to merge them again (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/28657), but until that happens, presumably we need to update that as well?

I am seeing this file is used in System.Runtime.Numeric only. it is even weird that this stored in the common folder. I guess that was the file we used in the globalization parsing before and it didn't get chance to be cleaned up. anyway, I'll add the fix to this file too.

Nit: add code comment explaining where this test came from. If we wanted to, we could even have a unit test that cycles through this entire list and ensures a hyphen matches every one of them. We have some unit test helper libraries that parse the Unicode data files, used primarily for Rune and StringInfo and S.T.E.W, but if there's interest we could also adapt it for this.

(Whether we should have a unit test that iterates through this really depends on whether this list is populated from one of the Unicode data files.)
I think I'm missing something, shouldn't this return true for regular hyphen \u002d? Even if it's not functionally necessary, it seems like a confusing method name if it doesn't return true for that.
Or maybe AllowAlternativeHyphenDuringParsing might be a better name?

No. If we have the negative sign as '-' then we don't need to do anything. The fix here is to allow parsing when using hyphen in the parsed string. when we have NegativeSign as hyphen it is already working today without any fix.

> Or maybe AllowAlternativeHyphenDuringParsing might be a better name?

No, we are allowing parsing the hyphen and not the alternative hyphens. 

The fix here is when having a culture using alternative hyphens as negative sign, we'll allow parsing strings using the hyphen 0+002D `-`.
Ah, you're quite right. I was thinking backwards.
